messages:
sam.support: FYI got a ticket from acme-inc — they say their org went to 0 credits ~3h before the expected monthly refill. Customer insists they did not spike usage. Can someone pull the token breakdown?

lia.billing: Assigned, pulling the billing export now. Do we have customer org id?

sam.support: org_acme_123 (reported CET). Customer mentioned heavy websocket streaming earlier in the day and multiple client reconnects.

lia.billing: Raw usage for that org (UTC):
```
2026-03-12T01:02:11Z  stream.tokens  1,200
2026-03-12T01:02:13Z  stream.tokens  1,150
2026-03-12T05:47:30Z  generate.tokens  320
2026-03-12T09:00:00Z  refill.attempt  N/A
2026-03-12T09:00:01Z  refill.success  0
```
Looks like a bunch of small streaming token events in bursts. Total tokens that day were within normal for them though — but the UI shows zeroed out earlier than expected.

max.eng: Two quick hypotheses: 1) burst window overlap + websocket reconnects caused duplication in our streaming token accounting (we have a PR that changed ephemeral session keys last month), 2) UI/tenant display cache updated before the actual refill job ran (race between refill job and cache invalidation).

sam.support: Customer screenshot shows wallet at 00:59 CET = 0, expected refill at 01:00 CET. They saw a 429 when starting a new call at 01:02.

lia.billing: Refill job in logs: 
```
2026-03-12T00:59:58Z refill: start tenant=org_acme_123
2026-03-12T00:59:59Z refill: compute delta -> +10000
2026-03-12T01:00:00Z refill: write succeed
```
But cache invalidation job: 
```
2026-03-12T01:00:00Z cache.invalidate tenant=org_acme_123 queued
2026-03-12T01:00:02Z cache.invalidate tenant=org_acme_123 done
```
So UI should show refill by 01:00:02 UTC — but customer claims 00:59 CET (00:59 local) was zero. Timezones could be confusing.

max.eng: Also check the streaming aggregator: if client reconnects, we previously had a case where partial session tokens were charged twice because the session id rotated but server-side dedupe key didn't persist across reconnects. Search for repeated session ids around 01:02.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0312-01 (investigate tenant visible-zero-before-refill). Assigned to max.eng.

max.eng: I pulled session logs. I see repeated ephemeral session tokens and a lot of small chunk events between 00:50-01:05 UTC. Example: 
```
[00:56:11Z] session_id=ephem_abc123 chunk.tokens=1
[00:56:12Z] session_id=ephem_abc123 disconnect
[00:56:12Z] session_id=ephem_def456 connect
[00:56:13Z] session_id=ephem_def456 chunk.tokens=1
```
That pattern could inflate counts if our per-chunk accounting doesn't dedupe within a short grace window. There's an open fix in staging to use a short-lived dedupe cache (30s) keyed by client_id+prompt_hash.

lia.billing: If the refill wrote successfully at 01:00:00Z, why did they see 429 at 01:02? Could their client be pinned to a stale token bucket from an older allocation?

max.eng: Two possibilities: the refill succeeded but the edge node serving their requests had a local in-memory bucket (pre-sharded) that wasn't updated until its poll (60s). That would make the user still see zero for up to polling interval. We're rolling a fix to push invalidations via pub/sub in <48h.

sam.support: Customer wants timeline and root cause. Can we confirm if their visible-zero was UI cache vs actual usage exhaustion?

lia.billing: Confirmed: usage ledger shows they did hit zero at 00:59:45Z due to burst of many tiny streaming chunks — ledger tokens were consumed. Refill then added credits at 01:00:00Z, but some edge nodes still thought bucket=0 until 01:00:45Z.

max.eng: Root cause: combination of (A) many short streaming reconnects that produced double-counted chunk events due to ephemeral session rotation, and (B) edge-level in-memory token buckets not invalidated immediately after refill. Action items: 1) Billing to issue a one-off credit to customer for duplicate counts (lia.billing), 2) Eng to backport session dedupe fix and push pub/sub cache invalidation for refill (max.eng), 3) Support to send timeline and apology (sam.support).

sam.support: I'll communicate the timeline and the planned mitigations. Draft message to customer: 
"Thanks — we traced this to duplicated streaming chunk accounting during frequent reconnects plus a delayed edge cache update; we've granted make-good credits and are shipping fixes to prevent recurrence. ETA for full fixes ~48h for cache push, 7d for dedupe backport; let me know if you need any logs."

lia.billing: I've queued the one-off credit and added a note on the billing case.

max.eng: Adding unit test to simulate reconnect storms. Also flagging for postmortem if we see similar tenant incidents in last 90d.

sam.support: Thanks team. I'll close the support ticket after customer ack. :thumbsup:
